title: Our Dreams at Dusk: Shimanami Tasogare
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In the seaside town of Onomichi, high schooler Tasuku Kaname is about to take his life after classmates find gay pornography on his phone and he fears being outed. He follows a mysterious figure called 'Someone' to a drop-in center whose members, including a lesbian couple, an older gay man, a trans man and a boy who likes wearing dresses, renovate abandoned houses together. Over four volumes Tasuku learns to accept himself among them.
life_message: It holds up being accepted as you are within a community that listens, as the way through shame and despair.

content.note: Everyday hostility and some violence against queer characters (Anime Feminist); level to verify.
Emotionally heavy: fear of exposure, family rejection, a partner's death without legal rights (Anime Feminist; Wikipedia; PW calls it raw).
Gay pornography on a phone triggers the plot; same-sex couples and crushes, no explicit content noted (Wikipedia; PW; MangaUpdates LGBT Scenes). PW notes it avoids fetishized portrayals.
Homophobic slurs and mockery from classmates (Wikipedia; Anime Feminist on queerphobia); frequency to verify.
Opens with Tasuku preparing to die by suicide; depression, internalized homophobia and bullying recur (Wikipedia; PW; Anime Feminist content warning; MangaUpdates Suicide/s; AniList Bullying 78%).
Outing and bullying shown as harmful; suicide attempt interrupted, framed toward support.

winners_losers: Tasuku and the drop-in community who accept one another win; classmates who mock and families who reject lose sympathy. The worldview favored is affirming of LGBTQ identity.
